headline: OCD Reports 7.7 Million People Affected by Recent Storms and Habagat
seoTitle: OCD: 7.7 Million Affected by Storms and Habagat | FMB News
seoDescription: The Office of Civil Defense says about 7.7 million people have been affected by recent tropical cyclones and Habagat, with assistance reaching about ₱1.42 billion.
deck: Around 2.2 million families have been affected, while 28,910 people remain in evacuation centers and authorities continue validating 31 reported deaths.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: The Office of Civil Defense reported on August 26 that about 7.7 million people, representing roughly 2.2 million families, have been affected by recent tropical cyclones and the southwest monsoon.

OCD said 346 evacuation centers were sheltering 8,446 families or 28,910 individuals. Authorities were validating reports of 31 deaths, while 19 people were reported injured and three remained missing.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: The affected population spans multiple regions, including Ilocos, Cagayan Valley, Central Luzon, Calabarzon, Mimaropa, Bicol, Western Visayas, Zamboanga Peninsula, the Cordillera Administrative Region and Metro Manila.
OCD placed the total cost of assistance at about ₱1.42 billion. It also estimated infrastructure damage at about ₱5.5 billion and agricultural damage at approximately ₱1.9 billion.

sections.heading: Why this matters
paragraphs: The figures show that the emergency remains a large-scale recovery operation even as weather conditions improve in some areas. Evacuation, damaged housing, disrupted livelihoods and infrastructure losses continue to require sustained national and local support.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: OCD and disaster agencies are continuing to validate casualty figures and damage assessments. Residents in affected areas should follow local government and PAGASA advisories as saturated ground and damaged infrastructure can remain hazardous after heavy rain subsides.
